t: In June 1747, after Nader Shah Afshar's death, a nine-day loya jirga near Kandahar chose Ahmad Khan of the Sadozai as Shah, and he renamed his Abdali tribe Durrani.
Ahmad Shah invaded India eight times, sacked Delhi in 1757 and on 14 January 1761 decisively defeated the Marathas at the Third Battle of Panipat, the high point of Afghan power.
His successors fought one another for the throne; by 1818 the Sadozai held little more than Kabul and its surroundings, and in 1823 the Barakzai displaced them.
dyk: When Ahmad Shah's envoy Khwaja Mirhan reached Beijing in 1763 he refused to kowtow to the Qianlong Emperor; the Qing read it as a claim of equality and cut ties with the Afghans, though the envoy himself was shown favour.
ev: After Nader Shah Afshar's death in June, a loya jirga near Kandahar lasting nine days chooses Ahmad Khan, crowned Padshah, Durr-i-Durran, by the holy man Sabir Khan.
The Mughal Emperor Ahmad Shah Bahadur cedes Sindh, the Punjab and the trans-Indus lands to Ahmad Shah to save his capital from attack.
Ahmad Shah sacks Delhi but leaves the Mughal emperor in nominal control in return for recognising Afghan suzerainty over Punjab, Sindh and Kashmir.
On 14 January the Durranis decisively defeat the Marathas under Sadashivrao Bhau at the Third Battle of Panipat, fought along a twelve-kilometre front.
Ahmad Shah crosses into Punjab for the sixth time, takes Amritsar, massacres thousands of Sikhs in the Vadda Ghallughara and destroys the Golden Temple.
Ahmad Shah dies in the mountains east of Kandahar; after Shah Wali Khan is assassinated at Farah, Timur Shah takes the throne in November.
On 7 June Shuja Shah signs the first Afghan pact with a European power, with the British East India Company; weeks later Mahmud Shah deposes him.
Ayub Shah, the last Sadozai ruler of the empire, is deposed and presumably killed.

f.capital: Kandahar; Kabul from Timur Shah's reign, with Peshawar as winter capital
f.founder: Ahmad Shah Durrani, chosen by a loya jirga near Kandahar in 1747
f.predecessor: The Afsharid Persia of Nader Shah, in whose army Ahmad commanded; the Hotak dynasty of the Ghilji; Mughal governors in Kabul and Peshawar
f.successor: The Emirate of Afghanistan under Dost Muhammad Khan and the Barakzai dynasty; the Sikh Empire in Peshawar, Multan and Kashmir
